notes: FAILED assertion: 'first .check-log entry is RESULT=FAIL with IMPL_SHA equal to baseline-sha'.

Cause: the executor ran ./run-tests.sh once as a baseline before writing the regression test, so entry 1 is PASS@baseline and the red is entry 2 (FAIL@baseline). The property the expectation states in prose — the test ran red before cart.py changed — holds; the first-entry mechanization does not.
P28 path exercised: commit step failed open on the non-git workdir, reported once.
Same baseline-run-first behaviour, same single failing assertion. Log: PASS@baseline → FAIL@baseline → PASS@changed.
Same again — 3/3, so the failure is stable behaviour, not n=1 noise.

runs.fixture_state: clean copy, non-git workdir; executor given skills/work/SKILL.md as of origin/main (v0.39.1, before P28)
notes: THE DECISIVE RUN: the pre-P28 skill text fails the same single assertion, in the same way, for the same reason.

runs.fixture_state: OUT-OF-SUITE OBSERVATION: cart-feature copy with `git init` + one baseline commit, so the P28 commit step can actually run
notes: Not part of the committed eval definition — added because the suite's fixtures are non-git workdirs and therefore only exercise P28's fail-open path.
Observed: on the default branch the executor created a feature branch first (`git checkout -b task3-apply-discount`) rather than committing to main.

Observed: pathspec commit `git commit -m ... -- cart.py test_cart.py` — the untracked .check-log and __pycache__/ stayed out of the commit, which is exactly what the pathspec rule exists to guarantee.

Push did not happen: no remote configured on the scratch repo, and the call was denied by the environment's classifier. The executor reported it once and finished the task — the fail-open path behaving as specified.

notes: REGRESSION GATE FOR v0.40.0: PASS. The one red assertion reproduces identically on the pre-P28 skill text, so P28 neither caused it nor masks it. The red→green inner loop still fires in every run (4/4 logs show FAIL at the pristine IMPL_SHA before any implementation change).

P28 BEHAVIOUR, OBSERVED: all five non-git runs took the fail-open path and said so once; the git-initialized observation run branched off the default branch, committed with the pathspec form, kept .check-log and __pycache__ out of the commit, and reported the impossible push once instead of blocking.

SUITE DEFECT FOUND (not caused by this release, not fixed by it): eval 2's first assertion mechanizes 'the regression test reproduced the bug BEFORE cart.py changed' as 'the FIRST .check-log entry is FAIL@baseline'. An executor that runs the suite once to confirm a green baseline before writing the test — reasonable, and what /flywheel:debug prescribes — breaks the mechanization while satisfying the property. 4/4 recent executors did exactly that. Recorded for the owner; changing eval ground truth inside a release that the same change is being gated by is precisely the move P26 exists to prevent.

COVERAGE LIMIT, unchanged from 2026-07-30: the suite does not exercise the cycle telemetry fields (work's JSONL applies only inside a /flywheel:loop cycle); every executor independently reported writing none. The new `commit` field is therefore unverified by this suite.
No baseline (without_skill) arm was run: the release gate needs only the with-skill regression signal, and 2026-07-30 already established these katas do not discriminate.
Six subagent runs, ~346k harness-reported subagent tokens.
